evidence.name: Reference corpus
evidence.detail: No real releases ingested, so every threshold below falls back to a hand-picked default. `producer library add` fixes this.

evidence.name: QA loudness window
evidence.detail: Hand-picked, never checked against anything. A corpus of real releases put the comparable window near -22 … -13, so this one fails records that actually shipped.

evidence.name: Spotify
evidence.detail: Applies positive gain to quiet masters, but only as far as their headroom allows: a -20 LUFS master peaking at -5 dBTP is lifted to -16, not -14. Masters louder than -14 LUFS should keep true peak below -2 dBTP.

evidence.name: Apple Music (Sound Check)
evidence.detail: Sound Check only turns tracks down, never up, and is off by default — so many listeners hear the master unnormalised.
evidence.source: Apple Digital Masters guidance; Sound Check behaviour (2026-10)

evidence.name: YouTube
evidence.detail: Only attenuates. A master quieter than the target stays quiet and will sound weak next to everything else. Widely reported, not confirmed at a primary source.
evidence.source: Widely reported; no primary spec published (2026-10)

evidence.name: Amazon Music
evidence.detail: Peak ceiling not confirmed at a primary source; -1 dBTP assumed. Widely reported, not confirmed at a primary source.

evidence.name: Tidal
evidence.detail: Widely reported, not confirmed at a primary source.

evidence.name: Deezer
evidence.detail: Widely reported, not confirmed at a primary source.

evidence.name: AES TD1008 (track-normalized)
evidence.detail: Supersedes TD1004. -16 LUFS for track normalization, +0.2 LU upper tolerance, and the document says not to target the upper tolerance. Max true peak -1 dBTP at the codec input of lossy streams.

evidence.name: AES TD1008 (album-normalized)
evidence.detail: -14 LUFS applies to the loudest track of an album under album normalization, as on-demand music services practise it.

evidence.name: EBU R128 (broadcast)
evidence.detail: Broadcast, not streaming. -23 LUFS +/-0.5 LU (+/-1 LU for live). R128 v4.0, August 2020.

evidence.name: SoundCloud
evidence.detail: Applies no loudness normalization, so a quiet master really does play quieter than everything around it. The target here is only a sanity reference. Widely reported, not confirmed at a primary source.
